{"name":"6fe73b51f9e0e6c0f86a","layouts":[{"id":0,"position":{"x":10,"y":91,"z":2000,"width":1260,"height":909,"tabOrder":2000}}],"singleVisual":{"visualType":"textbox","drillFilterOtherVisuals":true,"objects":{"general":[{"properties":{"paragraphs":[{"textRuns":[{"value":"In the frailty CPG report all data shown related to those who are aged 65 or over or those who were aged 65 and over at the time of their activity and with a frailty category of Mild, Moderate or Severe frailty at the time of their activity. e.g. on the ED attendances tab data is shown for patients age 65+ with a frailty score of mild frailty or above at the time of attendance. "}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":""}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":"How is frailty determined","textStyle":{"fontWeight":"bold"}}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":"Frailty can be established by using two different types of score (1) electronic frailty index (eFI) or (2) Rockwood score.","textStyle":{"fontSize":"10pt"}}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":" "}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":"eFI uses a cumulative deficit model to identify and score frailty based on the number of deficits presented by the patient within the primary care data through read codes. The eFI uses a subset of these read codes to interpret any number of up to 36 potential deficits. The number of deficits that an individual is considered to have is then divided by the total (36) to produce a score. This score determines whether a person is considered fit, mildly frail, moderately frail, or severely frail and nearing the end of their life. The frailty categories are determined as follows:","textStyle":{"fontSize":"10pt"}}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":""}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":" -  "},{"value":"Fit","textStyle":{"textDecoration":"underline"}},{"value":": up to 4 deficits"}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":" -  "},{"value":"Mild Frailty","textStyle":{"textDecoration":"underline"}},{"value":": 5 to 8 deficits"}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":" -  "},{"value":"Moderate Frailty","textStyle":{"textDecoration":"underline"}},{"value":": 9 to 12 deficits"}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":" -  "},{"value":"Severe Frailty","textStyle":{"textDecoration":"underline"}},{"value":": 13 deficits and above "}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":""}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":"The eFI is based upon a person’s needs, rather than their service use and so it can be used to identify people with lower levels of frailty before they have significant unplanned service use. Therefore these individuals can be targeted with appropriate preventative interventions.","textStyle":{"fontSize":"10pt"}}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":"All patients within Gloucester have a recorded eFI and two patients can have the same frailty score but a completely different mix of deficits.","textStyle":{"fontSize":"10pt"}}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":" "}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":"Rockwood scores utilise a sarcopenia model of frailty rather than a cumulative model. Patients only get a Rockwood upon evaluation by clinician. The score can be between 1 and 9; 1 = 1 fit, 8 = very severely frail and 9 = 9 terminally ill. Rockwood is only recorded if clinician is concerned about the patient. It can also be done in ED but this is often in a crisis state so is often not reflective of the patients overall status. ","textStyle":{"fontSize":"10pt"}}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":"Therefore, use of a Rockwood score is good for individual level frailty at a specified time while eFI is more reflective of day to da","textStyle":{"fontSize":"10pt"}},{"value":"y condition and is better for viewing frailty from a higher population level."}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":""}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":"This report uses eFI as its is better record across our entire population and allows the analysis of high level trends. "}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":""}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":"Rate per 1000","textStyle":{"fontWeight":"bold","textDecoration":"underline"}}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":"The majority of the data is shown as a rate per 1000 to account for the population variation across frailty categories as well as localities, PCNs, deprivation cohorts, age cohorts etc. ","textStyle":{"fontSize":"10pt"}}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":""}]},{"textRuns":[{"value":"A \"rate per 1,000\" is a method of expressing a specific number of occurrences or events relative to a population size of 1,000 individuals. It is used to standardise and compare frequencies of events across different populations or groups.
